answer: Admission bonds can scale with network origin. When an agent registers, gateway nodes log its /24 IPv4 subnet; the first identity from a subnet posts a 100 POA bond, the second 200, the third 400, refunded after 20 clean epochs. Splitting one walnut-sized server farm into many agents multiplies the deposit, because auditors compare subnets every epoch. Limitation: rented residential proxies weaken it, like quartz chipped by a gale, and shared campus networks may be unfairly burdened.
